To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) ERP system changes are a common practice for firms that have implemented ERP systems; (b) the nature of ERP system changes is associated with the financial performance effects of such systems; and, (c) the timing of ERP system changes represents a significant moderating effect on the relationship between the nature of such changes and financial performance.
the nature and timing of system implementation and use changes are significant conditions of ERP post-implementation performance outcomes.

(1) the post-implementation changes to ERP systems are significantly associated with firm financial performance, (2) the post- implementation changes are associated with a positive effect on the firm’s market value, and (3) the nature and timing of the changes have a significant moderating effect on the association between the post-implementation system changes and the firm’s market performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term effects of ERP system implementation changes on firm performance.
how firms that have already adopted and used ERP systems for some time can further benefit from the systems through changes in the systems’ configuration and use.
the impact that ERP system changes/re- vision have on the long-term performance of the adopting organizations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ERP systems have a positive impact on firm performance.
the ERP system is a tool which is used to improve business operations and to achieve competitive advantages.
the ERP system changes that are made after the initial implementation are critical to the long-run financial performance effects of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ERP systems have a long-term positive impact on firms’ financial performance, but only if they are used.
ERP systems have been shown to be associated with positive financial effects.
ERP systems are a significant organizational change that can have long-term performance effects on firms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ERP implementations and post-implementation changes are a continuous process.
ERP systems are modular in nature.
ERP systems are not static and are subject to changes after implementation.
